haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes from creation. A sweeper runs every minute and marks unclaimed HELD holds EXPIRED, freeing the stock. A claim also refuses lapsed holds.
haiku-low.q2: Before. Inventory checks every line first. If any line is short, it holds nothing, returns 409 with short SKUs, no charge is requested, and the cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is sent as the idempotency key, and retries reuse it, so the provider cannot charge twice.
haiku-low.q4: Payment is refunded in full through a refund row keyed by order id plus refund. The order is CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and the customer is emailed. Failed refunds are retried, then ops is alerted.
haiku-low.q5: Not emptied at Place order. After OrderConfirmed, Cart removes the snapshot lines. If checkout fails, the cart stays unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: NOT STATED as a single coordinator. Order sets order status through the steps. Cart checkout rows and Order's orders record progress with status.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment verifies it, writes an outbox row, and the relay publishes PaymentDeclined or PaymentSucceeded to the broker for Order.
haiku-low.q8: Payment stores the provider event id under a unique key, so repeats are spotted and ignored. Conditional updates match only the expected state. Consumers ignore repeated event ids.
haiku-low.q9: Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and calls Inventory to release the hold, triggered by the PaymentDeclined event. Inventory sets RELEASED and lowers reserved. If release fails, Order retries.
haiku-low.q10: By the claim result. If the hold is still HELD and unexpired, the claim succeeds and the order is confirmed. If it has lapsed, the full payment is refunded and the order cancelled.
haiku-low.q11: The refund row becomes FAILED, attempts increase, and the next try is set with backoff using the same refund key. It is tracked in Payment's refunds table. When attempts run out, ops is alerted.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, after Order confirms. Cart removes the snapshot lines, matched by line id and quantity.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes from creation. If not claimed in time, the hold lapses: the sweeper (runs every minute) marks it EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale (up to about a minute late); a claim also checks expires_at, so an expired hold cannot be claimed.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge is requested. If any line is short, Inventory holds nothing (all-or-nothing), returns 409 with the short SKUs, the order is REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, no charge is made, the cart is unchanged and the short items are shown.
sonnet.q3: The order id is used as the idempotency key; Payment retries with the same key on timeout or 5xx, so the provider cannot charge twice.
sonnet.q4: The order is set to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is fully refunded (Payment writes a refund row and calls the provider), and the customer is emailed that the refund is in progress. No partial orders.
sonnet.q5: The cart is not emptied at Place order. It is cleared only after the order is CONFIRMED (Cart removes the snapshot lines on OrderConfirmed). On failure (short stock, decline, late success) the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q6: NOT STATED as a single orchestrator. The doc describes a choreographed saga: Order calls Inventory and Payment over HTTP and reacts to broker events (PaymentDeclined/PaymentSucceeded), with Cart and Order status rows. Progress is recorded in Order's order status (e.g. PLACING, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED), with Cart's checkout row (status, attempt id, order id) and Payment's payment/refund rows tracking their parts.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment verifies it, updates the payment row, and via the outbox relay publishes PaymentDeclined or PaymentSucceeded on the broker. Order consumes that event and finishes the order.
sonnet.q8: Payment stores the provider's event id under a unique key, so a repeated webhook is spotted, answered 200 and ignored with no state change or event. A conditional update from AWAITING_WEBHOOK means a repeated success matches nothing, so no second event is published. On the broker, consumers ignore events by event id and act only when the row is in the expected state.
sonnet.q9: The PaymentDeclined event triggers Order to set PAYMENT_DECLINED and call Inventory to release the hold. Inventory sets it RELEASED and lowers reserved, so the stock is back on sale. If the release fails, Order retries, and the hold expires after 10 minutes anyway with the sweeper freeing the stock.
sonnet.q10: At claim time, Inventory changes the hold to CLAIMED only if it is still HELD and not expired. If it claims, the order is confirmed; if the hold is expired (EXPIRED returned), the order is cancelled and refunded in full. The design never keeps money for an order it cannot fulfil.
sonnet.q11: The refund row becomes FAILED, the attempt count goes up, and a retry is scheduled with backoff using the same refund key. When attempts run out, ops is alerted and the row stays open for a reconciliation job. The pending refund is tracked in Payment's refund row (status, attempts, next attempt time), which is never deleted.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, published by Order after the claim succeeds, causes the Cart service to remove the snapshot lines from the cart, matched by line id and quantity. Items added during checkout stay.
